Secondary source (darwinexzero.document360.io/docs/risk-engine): direct curl looped in an infinite redirect (bot/JS-challenge protection on that CDN) and could not be captured with raw byte/hash evidence this session; its claims below were extracted via the WebFetch tool's rendered-content pass instead and are labelled with a weaker evidentiary tier accordingly.
profile: Darwinex Zero DARWIN Risk Engine (applies to all live DARWIN-tracked strategies, independent of FTMO/prop-firm rules)

sources.capture_note: curl -L against this URL looped past 50 redirects this session (document360's CDN likely gates on a JS/cookie challenge that curl cannot satisfy); raw response evidence unavailable. Claims below came from a same-session WebFetch tool call against the identical URL, which renders JS and returned readable content -- but WebFetch does not expose the underlying HTTP status/bytes/hash, so this source cannot be verified byte-for-byte the way the primary source above can.

normalized_claims.target_var_selection_rule: target VaR moves within [3.25%, 6.5%] based on a historical volatility ratio computed over up to a 6-month lookback, with the engine tolerating up to a 2x (up or down) change in VaR before adjusting the target
normalized_claims.leverage_formula: Lev(investor) = Lev(trader) x (target_VaR / strategy_VaR) x f
normalized_claims.strategy_var_lookback_qualifier: last 45 days in which the trader remained exposed to the market (not 45 calendar days)
risk_adjustment_trigger_points: at trade initiation: position size calculated to meet the target monthly VaR
during an open position: a second-level risk adjustment may be applied if a D-Leverage threshold is approached, independent of the initiation-time sizing
normalized_claims.no_fixed_drawdown_or_trading_restriction: Darwinex Zero states there is no fixed trading-rule set (no max daily loss %, no max total loss %, no minimum trading days) the way FTMO has -- risk is governed entirely through the VaR-targeting Risk Engine and D-Leverage caps above, not through static drawdown gates. This is a structural difference from the FTMO rulepack in this same evidence set and must not be conflated with it in any shared cost/risk model.

d_leverage_bucket_boundary_discrepancy.finding: The two official sources for the same short-hold D-Leverage=16.25 bucket disagree on its upper time boundary.
d_leverage_bucket_boundary_discrepancy.both_sources_agree_on: the mid bucket is exactly [30, 60) minutes at D-Leverage 13, and the long-hold bucket is more than 60 minutes at D-Leverage 9.75
d_leverage_bucket_boundary_discrepancy.resolution: NOT_RESOLVED_BY_THIS_SNAPSHOT -- recorded verbatim from both sources per the hard_constraint against inventing/reconciling values without a documented source. Since QM's own >60-minute D-Leverage figure already in use (see project memory reference_venue_cost_model / 9.75% leverage) is unaffected by this discrepancy (both sources agree on 9.75 for the long-hold bucket QM actually operates in), this does not block current usage, but the exact <15min-vs-<30min boundary should not be relied on for any sub-30-minute strategy without a fresh, disambiguating check.
d_leverage_bucket_boundary_discrepancy.owner_attention_needed: Only if QM ever designs a strategy intended to hold positions between 15 and 30 minutes, where the two sources would classify the D-Leverage cap differently (16.25 vs the 13 mid-bucket).
